A huge turbine that grows with its size. Count its sections: width × height ÷ 9 × length (a 3×3×3 is 3, a 7×9×15 is 105). It takes up to 40 mB/t of steam per section, at {fe:20}, {fe:36} or {fe:56} FE per mB of Steam, High-Pressure or Superheated Steam. A 7×9×15 on Superheated Steam makes {fe:235200} FE/t before its bonuses.
Its output cap is a full flow of Superheated Steam with both bonuses, and it holds 400 ticks of that; its energy ports share the cap.
Its rotor spins up over a few seconds when steam flows, and the output rises with it. The better the steam, the faster it spins.
Build a hollow tube on either horizontal axis: a cross-section 3 to 7 wide and 3 to 9 tall, 3 to 15 long. In a 3×3 tube only the corners must be casings; in a bigger one all twelve edges must be. Its front is the side with the most glass (or the side you finish it from). A new turbine starts with a steam, an energy and an Exhaust port on its fitted spots (see below); move or clear them with the Wrench (see Conduits & the Wrench).
Heavy Oil or Seed Oil in its lubricant tank (4,000 mB, through a lubricant port) adds 8% to its output and doubles how fast the rotor spins up, using 1 mB a second per 3 sections.
# The turbine-generator set
Formed, its blocks disappear into one turbine-generator set along its axis, on a steel plinth: from the steam end, turbine casings on one shaft with bearing pedestals and couplings between them, then the generator at the far end (the positive end of its axis) with its cooling ribs and terminal box. 3 to 5 long it has one turbine casing; 6 to 9 a small high-pressure and a large low-pressure casing; 10 to 15 high-, intermediate- and a double-flow low-pressure casing, with a crossover pipe arching from the intermediate into the low-pressure casing. The casings fill the cross-section's shorter side; a cross-section wider than tall gets a walkway along its front. The window on each side of a casing shows its rotor turning.
Ports fit best where the machine meets them: a steam port on top, over the high-pressure casing's steam chest; an energy port on the generator end; an Exhaust port underneath, under the low-pressure casing's exhaust neck, where a Condenser Array can sit. A new turbine starts with a port on each. Jade names the section you look at and these spots. A port anywhere else still gets a pipe from the machine out to it.
# Exhaust
With an Exhaust port (a new turbine has one underneath) spent steam leaves as Exhaust Steam instead of venting. While it drains (its exhaust tank isn't full) the turbine makes 10% more FE, on top of lubricant. Clear the Exhaust port and it vents.
